title: A Wolf for the Spire
premise: Jude Lockridge has spent her life copying prayers in a valley where magic cannot follow, bound by her mother's debts to the Temple of the Quiet Flame. When the old gods stir beneath the mountain and begin answering prayers again, Jude discovers her own name in an ancient contract: her soul was sold before her birth to the court beneath the mountain. To reclaim it, she must leave the valley — where magic floods back into her blood and awakens something she was never meant to be. As she descends through a world of debt-collectors, god-touched rebels, and a spire that eats memories, she learns justice for the sold is not found in any law but must be taken. In the end, Jude confronts the god who brokered her sale, refuses both his bargain and his throne, and rewrites the contract itself — freeing every soul held beneath the mountain at the cost of her own magic, which drains away as she walks home to a valley that can finally hold all of her.
about_author: Jonah Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing legal contracts from defunct monasteries, an experience that left a permanent fascination with what people sign away. They write fantasy about paperwork, power, and the people caught between them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes daily life: copying prayers that never get answered, the temple's ledgers of debt, and the invisible boundary at the valley's edge where birds turn back. Jude quietly falsifies one ledger entry to save a child from indenture. Emotional beat: restless compassion trapped inside rigid order.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A dying widow's prayer is answered for the first time in three hundred years — a candle relights itself mid-copying. The temple elders panic and seal the scriptorium. Jude feels the words on the page move under her fingers. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. An envoy from beneath the mountain arrives to collect on an old contract bearing Jude's mother's signature — and Jude's name. She has until the moon completes its thirteenth turn. The temple, eager to be rid of a troublemaker, pays her passage instead of protecting her. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution she served.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She steps over the valley boundary; magic crashes into her like cold water, and the world sharpens into colors and voices she's never perceived. Her first act of accidental magic nearly kills her guide. Emotional beat: terror and intoxication intertwined.

chapters.title: The Debt-Collector's Road
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with interludes from the envoy Vess. On the road, Jude sees how the old gods' return has weaponized faith: villages tithing children to shrines. Vess reveals he is not her captor but her assigned witness — court protocol demands one. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance forming.

chapters.title: What Her Mother Signed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In a waystation archive, Jude reads the original contract: her mother sold not only Jude's soul but her name-before-birth, meaning Jude has lived her whole life under a borrowed identity. Emotional beat: identity shaken to its foundation.

chapters.title: The God-Touched
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Rebels who channel fragments of the waking gods ambush the caravan, mistaking Jude for a court agent. Their leader, Sefa, recognizes the mark of the sold on Jude and offers sanctuary. Emotional beat: belonging offered by strangers for the first time.

chapters.title: Learning to Burn
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Among the rebels, Jude trains her raw magic; it responds to language — she casts by rewriting reality like a ledger. But each working erases a memory she chooses to feed it. Emotional beat: power's seductive price made literal.

chapters.title: Vess's Testimony
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. He records his official observations but privately doubts the court's right to collect souls bought from desperate mothers. Flashback to his own sister, sold generations ago. Emotional beat: conscience stirring inside a functionary.

chapters.title: The Shrine That Ate a Village
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The rebels raid a shrine hoarding answered prayers; Jude finds souls stored like grain and frees one — a child's — against Sefa's orders, alerting the court to their position. Emotional beat: mercy with consequences.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Sefa confesses the rebellion's true aim: not freedom, but to seize the spire's contract-magic and rule. She offers Jude a place beside her if Jude helps steal the master ledger. Emotional beat: disillusionment — justice outside the law can corrupt too.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Captured by the court after the raid, Jude is brought underground to a cathedral of filing-cabinets and whispering clerks-gods. She meets the Broker, the god who drafts all soul-contracts, courteous and terrible. Emotional beat: awe weaponized into dread.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Broker offers a deal: serve as his scribe for a century and keep her soul. He shows her the master ledger — every prayer ever answered has a price column. Jude pretends to consider while memorizing the ledger's structure. Emotional beat: playing powerless while planning.

chapters.title: The Spire of Names
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Escorted to the spire where sold souls are kept as ink, Jude finds her mother — alive, aged backward, serving as the Broker's first scribe, complicit for decades. Emotional beat: the reunion she wanted becoming the confrontation she feared.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Confession
chapters.summary: Mother's POV (interleaved with Jude's). The truth: Jude's father was a god, and the sale was protection — hiding Jude's nature from the other gods, not greed. The thirteenth moon ends the hiding. Emotional beat: love expressed as an unforgivable lie.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns Complete
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The moon fills; Jude's hidden divinity ignites, and the court moves to enthrone her as their new face — a god they can file and control. Sefa's rebels breach the mountain simultaneously, forcing a three-way war in the deep halls. Emotional beat: everyone wants to own her.

chapters.title: The Ledger War
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Battle through the archive-cathedral: Sefa's forces burning contracts, the court counter-writing reality, Jude rewriting lines faster than either side. Vess turns his testimony against the court, reading aloud the crimes recorded in their own files. Emotional beat: chaos as liberation begins.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the climax, the Broker offers her everything: her soul, her mother freed, the rebels spared — if she takes his desk and becomes the new Broker. She sees clearly how power preserves itself by recruiting its victims. Emotional beat: the temptation of righteous tyranny.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude refuses — and instead of destroying the ledger, she amends it: striking the enforcement clauses, voiding all sales made under desperation, including her own. The Broker unravels without contracts to enforce, and the spire begins to collapse. Emotional beat: triumph that costs everything.

chapters.title: Ash and Ink
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Escape from the falling spire; her mother chooses to stay with the dissolving souls rather than return to a world that moved on. Vess carries out the amended ledger as legal precedent. Jude's magic burns away with the spire, leaving her mortal. Emotional beat: grief braided with release.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Home
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She travels back through a changed land — shrines empty, debts uncollectable, the god-touched ordinary again. Sefa, stripped of stolen power, watches her pass without a word. Jude writes her own name — her real one — for the first time. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning.

chapters.title: A Wolf for the Spire
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Home in the valley, now open to the world, Jude runs the temple as a school where no one signs anything. A wolf — the last fragment of the Broker, or perhaps just a wolf — sits at the valley line, watching, and she lets it stay. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, identity finally whole.
